records.question: How long did the project on Rose Atoll last?
ground_truth_chunks: A six week project, jointly funded by the Department of Marine and Wildlife Resources (DMWR), the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USF&W), and Office of Development Planning was conducted to eradicate the rat population on Rose Atoll.

records.question: On what dates were nightly surveys conducted on Rose Island?
records.ground_truth_answer: Nightly surveys were conducted from 18 October to 28 November, 1990.
ground_truth_chunks: Nightly surveys were conducted on Rose Island from 18 October to 28 November, 1990.

records.question: What species were all turtles seen during the study?
records.ground_truth_answer: All turtles seen during the study were green turtles (Chelonia mydas).
ground_truth_chunks: All turtles seen during the study, both hatchling and adult, were green turtles (Chelonia mydas).

records.question: According to the RECOMMENDATIONS section, what data should be maintained so pit counts can be used to estimate egg-bearing nests?
records.ground_truth_answer: Maintain data on the number of false pits dug per nest for each witnessed nesting event, and apply that ratio to future pit counts to get a rough indicator of egg-bearing nests.
ground_truth_chunks: If the ratio of blank pits to actual nests remains constant over the years, pit counts can be used as a relative index of abundance, but not as indicator of successful nesting.

However, if data were maintained on the number of false pits dug per nest for each witnessed nesting event, that ratio could be applied to future pit counts to get a rough indicator of egg-bearing nests.
